prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas, and has neck and back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1371; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on a recording, so just call me the claimant.

Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were and what you were doing when the collision happened?

A: I was driving home from work in Pearland, heading down a two-lane road. It was a slow stretch, maybe thirty miles an hour, and traffic was light.

Q: Can you tell me what happened next?

A: A car came over into my lane. I braked and swerved a little, but we still ended up nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit. The airbags didn't go off, but I felt a jolt through my whole body.

Q: Did you lose consciousness or hit your head?

A: No, I stayed awake and didn't hit my head. I just felt shaken up.

Q: Did you get out of the vehicle and seek any medical attention?

A: I got out and felt okay for about an hour. Then my neck started stiffening up, and my lower back began to ache. I went to an urgent care clinic that evening.

Q: What did the medical provider tell you?

A: They diagnosed a neck strain and a lower back strain. They gave me some muscle relaxers and told me to rest and use ice and heat.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes, the neck pain is worse when I turn my head to check traffic, and I'm having trouble sitting for long periods because of my back.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want my treatment to be covered.

Q: Understood. Thank you for your time.
